newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Arafat, Israel defence chief speak by phone.
newsitem.headline: Arafat, Israel defence chief speak by phone.

text.p: Palestinian President Yasser Arafat and Israel's Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai spoke by telephone on Sunday and agreed to meet soon, an Israeli official said.
"During the conversation, which was conducted in a positive atmosphere, both men decided to meet soon, after Arafat returns from a visit to Japan," Mordechai's spokesman said in a statement.

Arafat is due to travel on Monday to Japan where he will brief government officials on his landmark summit last Wednesday with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and discuss bilateral relations.
Netanyahu announced after his talks with Arafat that Mordechai would meet the Palestinian leader on Sunday.
But a Palestinian official said on Saturday the meeting had been postponed because both men had busy schedules.
"A final date for the meeting will be set soon," the spokesman said. "They will discuss a series of security matters on the agenda between Israel and the Palestinian Authority."
Mordechai has been formulating Israeli plans for a long-delayed troop redeployment in the West Bank town of Hebron.

Israel has said new security arrangements are needed to protect 400 Jewish settlers living among more than 100,000 Palestinians in Hebron. The Palestinians want Israel to implement unchanged a partial pullout agreed by its previous government.
